issues.legal_issue: A bail application involving alleged MCOCA offences must be considered by applying the statutory restrictions on bail under Section 21(4), rather than by assessing the sufficiency or correctness of the prosecution evidence.
A court deciding bail must not make definitive findings on the accused’s roles in the alleged crime, since those matters are for determination at trial.
A bail order that lacks the required consideration under Section 21(4) of MCOCA and makes impermissible findings on the merits is liable to be set aside and reconsidered.
